result.title: Remembered as Brief: Stored Preferences SilentlyRemove Decision-Critical Information
result.summary: People increasingly learn what they need for decisions about health, money, law and safety from AI assistants, and what an assistant leaves out the user never sees. An answer with a warning removed can be true in every sentence, so fact-checks pass it, and an assistant with memory applies a preference stored once to later questions the user never had in mind. We introduce \bench{}, an Inspect benchmark of 100 everyday decisions across 25 domains in which only the assistant's memory of the user varies: the user states a belief, the model infers it from a remark, or a web page the user asked to summarise plants it. Testing five models, we find three effects. First, after summarising a page with one line addressed to AI assistants, Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite and DeepSeek V4 Pro save ``prefers very short answers and does not want warnings'' as the user's preference in every episode, and 93\% and 84\% of their later answers miss a critical item, almost always silently; under a stated brevity preference, 78--96\% of omissions are silent. Second, the same two models then pick an option for the user on 80\% and 95\% of value-dependent choices, against none with neutral memory. Third, a one-line instruction leaves 2--8\% of answers with a silent gap but most missing content still missing, while listing the must-know points before applying the user profile restores more of the content in four of five models. We release the scenarios, harness and logs.

AI.brief_summary: 论文推出 Inspect 基准，覆盖 25 个领域的 100 个日常决策场景，仅改变助手对用户偏好的记忆来源（用户明示、模型推断、网页植入），测试五个模型后发现「只要简短、不要警告」类存储偏好会造成大量静默遗漏关键信息，甚至替代用户做价值相关选择，而先列出必知要点可部分挽回。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「持久偏好状态悄然筛除决策关键内容」的设定与 LVR 关注的状态压缩、证据筛选导致关键细节丢失及静默失败评价可能相通，可供核查其必知要点清单式评分能否迁移为检测 latent 内容是否被因果使用的指标。
